_note: Typed absence for the intelligence surface (error-system.md; local-ai-engine.md §4.3, §4.12). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: the module NEVER fakes a result. Every way the capability can be missing has its own code and its own reason, and each answer says which one it is: the engine is not in this build; the child module that serves a modality is excluded (a cascade tells you which parent took it); no model is installed; the named model is unknown; the build cannot serve the entry's format; the target reaches the surface but does not run inference. The reach-vs-run law (§4.12) is the point of the last one: EVERY target may call `dsx.module.intelligence.*` and gets service or a typed absence with a reason, never silence and never a lie. Absence is also never a crash — constitution Article 7.

cases.name: absence: no engine in this build answers not_available with a reason
cases._note: The app dropped the module weight. The call still resolves — typed — so a surface can offer the download or hide the feature honestly.

cases.name: absence: an excluded provider child answers with its cascade reason
cases._note: The voice child is excluded from this build, so `synthesize` on `intelligence.voice` is absent — and the answer names the chain and the exclusion reason, which is exactly what `despia.excluded` publishes on the page side. A UI can say 'this app was built without voice', not 'something went wrong'.

cases.name: absence: a cascade-excluded child reports the parent that took it
absence: no model installed is its own answer, not an engine failure
cases._note: The engine is present and healthy; the device simply has nothing downloaded. `no_model_available` is the code a first-run UI keys its download prompt off.

cases.name: absence: an unknown model id is refused typed and names the id
absence: an entry whose engine this build lacks is unsupported, not broken
cases._note: The catalog is a fleet-wide document and a given build carries a given set of backends. An entry naming a backend this build does not carry answers `unsupported` — the registry-not-enum law (§4.2) seen from the caller's side.

cases.name: absence: a reach-only target is served the reason, never silence
cases._note: The reach-vs-run law (§4.12). The watch declares no inference; the call still lands on the bus and comes back typed with `run_not_declared` plus the target — which is what lets a watch app show 'open this on your phone' instead of a spinner that never resolves.

cases.name: absence: an unserved locale answers fit-shaped, so the UI can offer the download
cases._note: A voice request for a language no installed voice serves is not a failure of TTS — it is a missing asset, and the answer carries the language plus the catalog ids that WOULD serve it (§4.9).
